region: Watkins Glen · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Lakewood Vineyards sits on the west shore of Seneca Lake, a few miles north of Watkins Glen. Frank and Lucy Stamp bought a run-down peach and apple orchard here in 1951 and planted grapes the next spring, and for decades the family sold its fruit to juice companies and larger wineries. In 1988 they made their first wine from their own grapes, bottling it the following May. Today three generations of Stamps run the place, with Chris Stamp as winemaker and his son Ben focusing on the winery’s sparkling wines.

Bubbly Catawba is made from free-run juice of Catawba, one of America’s oldest wine grapes. Catawba was identified in the Carolinas around 1801 and became the foundation of early American wine: in Cincinnati, Nicholas Longworth turned it into a Champagne-style sparkler that made Ohio the country’s leading wine state by the 1850s. The Finger Lakes and Lake Erie hold most of the plantings today. The grape’s dusky pink-red skins carry little colour, so it naturally gives pale rosé wines.

Catawba also has a Finger Lakes sparkling story of its own. In the 1940s Charles Fournier, a Champagne-trained winemaker at Gold Seal, found a paler mutation of the grape in his vineyards and used this “Pink Catawba” for sparkling wine; in 1950 it became the first wine from outside California to win gold at the California State Fair. Lakewood calls Bubbly Catawba a fruity take on America’s original sparkling wine, spritzy and sweet-tart. Reviewing the 2022, Decanter found raspberry candy, allspice and clove, then sweet cherry on a light, off-dry palate.
